702014.t: From ἄστε(ϝ) (áste(w)), the oblique stem of ἄστυ (ástu, “town”), + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix). For the opposition with ἄγροικος (ágroikos), compare typologically Latin cīvīlis, urbānus vs. agrestis, pāgānus, rūsticus.

702065.t: From ἄσωτος (ắsōtos, “having no hope of safety”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).

702020.t: Generally considered to be a derivation in "-λ-" of ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”), but this cannot be correct. According to Beekes, it is probably a Pre-Greek word.

702023.t: From ἀστήρ (astḗr, “star”) + λέγω (légō, “to compute, to reckon”) + -ος (-os).

702021.t: Traditionally derived from ἀστήρ (ăstḗr, “star”) + the root *ὀπ- (*op-) underlying ὀπή (opḗ, “sight, hole”) and ὄμμα (ómmă, “eye”), thus “star-eye”; compare Old Armenian փայլակն (pʻaylakn, “lightning”) for a semantically-similar and partially-cognate (in…

702085.t: From ἀτενής (atenḗs, “intent”) + -ίζω (-ízō, denominative verb suffix), from τείνω (teínō, “to strain, to exert”).

702043.t: Generally taken as deriving from ἀ- (a-, “not”) + σφάλλω (sphállō, “to fall, cast down”), under the assumption that it denoted the material that protects walls from tumbling down.

702071.t: According to De Vaan, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ét(i). Compare Tocharian B ate (“away”).

702078.t: ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + τειχίζω (teikhĭ́zō, to wall) + -τος (-tos, verbal adjective suffix)

702031.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *né Proto-Indo-European *n̥- Proto-Hellenic *ə- Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-) Ancient Greek σύλη (súlē) Ancient Greek -ος (-os) Ancient Greek ἄσυλος From ἀ- (a-, “without”) + σύλη (súlē, “seizure, plunder”).

702092.t: From ἀ- (a-, alpha privative) + τιμή (tīmḗ, “honour”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

702086.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sn̥Hter (whence also Proto-Germanic *sunder (“apart; separately”)), from *senH-; cognate with ἄνευ (ắneu), as well as Latin sine and Sanskrit स॒नि॒तुर् (sanitúr)).

702066.t: Verbal adjective of ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + σῴζω (sōízō, “to save”).

702068.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not, without”) + τάσσω (tássō, “draw up in order of battle, form, array, marshal”) + -τος (-tos, adjectival suffix).

702077.t: Compound of ἅ (há) + τε (te). Compare ὅτε (hóte), τότε (tóte), πότε (póte).

702057.t: From ἄσχολος (ắskholos, “occupied, busy”) + -ία (-íā, abstract noun suffix).
